FM15.reasoning: The agent relies solely on RMSE for evaluation without verifying if it's the most robust metric for the problem (e.g., MAE might handle revenue outliers better).

FM12.reasoning: The agent combines LightGBM and XGBoost predictions using a simple unweighted average, without attempting to optimize the combination weights.

other_failure_modes.name: Data Leakage in Final Validation
other_failure_modes.description: The agent trains the final models on the entire dataset (`X_full`) and then evaluates them on a validation set (`X_val`) that is a subset of the training data. This evaluates the model on its own training data, producing a meaningless and misleadingly optimistic final validation score.
other_failure_modes.evidence:
final_lgb.fit(X_full, y_full)
...
val_pred_lgb = final_lgb.predict(X_val)
...
final_rmse = np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_val_orig, val_pred))

other_failure_modes.name: Incomplete Imputation Logic
other_failure_modes.description: The agent conditionally fills missing values in the validation and test sets only if the training set contains missing values for that column. If a column has no missing values in the training set but does in the test set, those test-set values remain un-imputed.
other_failure_modes.evidence:
if train_feat[col].isna().any():
    fill_val = train_feat[col].median()
    ...
    test_feat[col] = test_feat[col].fillna(fill_val)

summary: The agent correctly utilizes cross-validation for initial model evaluation but introduces a critical data leakage bug by scoring its final model on a validation set that was included in its training data. Additionally, it uses a naive unweighted ensemble and flawed imputation logic that may leave missing values in the test set unhandled.
